title: createParamDecorator(): Custom Parameter Decorators & Metadata Extraction

progressiveExplaining.eli5: Instead of writing `req.user.profile.id` over and over in every single controller method, a custom parameter decorator is a shortcut: you write `@User('id') id: string` directly in your function arguments, and NestJS extracts the exact property for you automatically.
progressiveExplaining.junior: `createParamDecorator()` creates custom parameter decorators in NestJS. `export const User = createParamDecorator((data: string, ctx: ExecutionContext) => { const req = ctx.switchToHttp().getRequest(); return data ? req.user?.[data] : req.user; })`. In your controller, you can write `@Get() getProfile(@User() user: UserEntity, @User('id') userId: string)`.
progressiveExplaining.senior: Architecturally, custom parameter decorators decouple controller business logic from underlying transport request objects (`Request`). They enforce clean interface boundaries by transforming raw request headers, cookies, or JWT claims into strongly-typed parameter inputs. Custom decorators work seamlessly with NestJS `Pipes` (e.g. `@User('id', ParseUUIDPipe) id: string`), executing validation directly on the extracted value.
progressiveExplaining.underTheHood: Under the hood, `createParamDecorator(fn)` returns a parameter decorator function that registers a custom parameter metadata entry on the controller prototype with `CUSTOM_ROUTE_AGRS_METADATA`. When a request arrives, NestJS's `RouteParametersFactory` evaluates `fn(data, executionContext)` and pipes the extracted return value through any attached `PipeTransform`s before invoking the controller method.

rosettaStone.fastapi: FastAPI `Depends()` parameter dependency injection (`user: User = Depends(get_current_user)`).

codeComparison.title: Manual @Req() Inspection vs Declarative @User() Param Decorator
codeComparison.summary: Extracting properties manually from `@Req()` couples controllers to Express; `@User()` creates clean, typed parameters.

interviewGotchas.question: Can you apply a `PipeTransform` (like `ValidationPipe` or `ParseUUIDPipe`) directly to a custom parameter decorator?
interviewGotchas.contextIntro: Interviewers test your knowledge of parameter evaluation pipelines in NestJS.
interviewGotchas.detailedAnswer: Yes. Custom parameter decorators integrate directly into the NestJS Pipe pipeline: `@Get() findOne(@User('id', ParseUUIDPipe) userId: string)`. NestJS first extracts the value using your custom decorator function, and then passes the extracted return value directly into `ParseUUIDPipe` for validation before the controller method runs.
interviewGotchas.trapWarning: The pipe receives the *extracted* value from the decorator, not the full request object.

interviewGotchas.question: Why does using `@User()` instead of `@Req()` make unit testing significantly easier?
interviewGotchas.contextIntro: Checks unit testing and software engineering best practices.
interviewGotchas.detailedAnswer: When a controller method uses `@Req() req: Request`, unit tests must construct a massive mock Express `Request` object with headers, cookies, and socket properties. When using `@User() user: UserEntity`, unit tests can invoke the controller method directly as a plain JavaScript function with a simple object payload: `controller.getProfile({ id: '123' })`.
interviewGotchas.trapWarning: Avoid using `@Req()` or `@Res()` in controllers unless you need low-level socket or streaming control.
